title: Screwball Comedy
objective: After this level you can explain why fast-talking screwball comedies of the 1930s pitted sharp-witted couples against each other.
summary: Screwball comedies paired mismatched lovers who fought in fast, overlapping dialogue. Depression audiences wanted people beating adversity, and the Hays Code swapped sex for sparring.

cards.headline: In 1934, a comedy about a runaway heiress swept the Oscars.
cards.body: Frank Capra's It Happened One Night follows a runaway heiress and the reporter who tracks her down. It became the first film to win all five major Academy Awards, and it helped set the rules for a new kind of comedy: the screwball. Why would a love story work best as a fight?

cards.headline: Mismatched, and made for each other
cards.body: Screwball comedies put seemingly mismatched lovers at the center of unlikely romances, surrounded by off-the-wall characters and zany situations. In Bringing Up Baby (1938), Katharine Hepburn's eccentric heiress pursues Cary Grant's bookish paleontologist through one farcical mishap after another. The couples are often elegantly dressed in Art Deco rooms, and their shared talent for mischief is the proof they belong together.

cards.headline: Talk fast, and talk over each other
cards.body: Director Howard Hawks made overlapping dialogue one of his trademarks, and His Girl Friday (1940) is famous for its rapid-fire delivery. Hawks took The Front Page, a story about a newspaper editor and his reporter, and changed the pair from two men to a man and a woman: Cary Grant and Rosalind Russell. Now every argument about the job was also an argument about the two of them.

cards.headline: Why all the arguing?
cards.body: During the Depression, with film attendance in decline, studios wanted stories that showed people triumphing over adversity. They also had a rulebook. The Hays Code, Hollywood's own guidelines from 1934 to 1968, banned explicit mention of sexual relationships. So, as Britannica puts it, verbal sparring and physical comedy took the place of sexuality. In a screwball comedy, the quarrel is the love scene.

questions.prompt: Why did screwball couples trade insults and pratfalls instead of playing open love scenes?

options.label: The Hays Code banned sexual references; sparring stood in
Depression audiences wanted no romance at all in their comedies
options.rationale: Audiences wanted stories of people beating adversity, romance included.

options.label: Sound equipment couldn't record quiet scenes
options.rationale: Sound wasn't the limit; the Hays Code banned sexual references.

options.rationale: The limit came from Hollywood's own code.
